authority: Existing repository obligations and the owner-authorized comparison intent; unresolved policy remains proposed.
provenance: The planner wrote expected effects from explicit event timelines and simple counted inputs, without executing a bridge or calling its helpers. The implementation agent must review them independently against canonical requirements before binding executable fixtures.

interpretation.events: Domain-level descriptions, not an implemented HTTP or test-runner API.
interpretation.symbols: A/B/C and session-alpha/session-beta are synthetic aliases. A fixture adapter may instantiate valid wire identifiers but cannot derive expected ownership, ordering or counts from candidate output.
interpretation.order: Sequence is durable acceptance order inside one browser queue; separate profiles do not promise a global click order.
interpretation.ambiguity: A lost response does not establish whether commit occurred. Retry must reconcile using the original submission identity.
interpretation.durability: Examples cover bridge process restart with a functioning OS/filesystem. OS/power-loss durability is a separate predeclared policy.
interpretation.effect: Exactly one stored work item is distinct from watcher notifications or LLM executions.
interpretation.review: These examples are independent design inputs, not owner approval of every new numeric target. Scenario mappings point back to the canonical plan.

events: Accept A durably in the browser queue
Commit A and its receipt in the bridge
Drop the acceptance reply
Restart bridge and browser worker
Retry the exact original A
cases.rejected_counterexample: Two stored records, a changed retry identity, an uncommitted success or a cleared queue before a validated receipt.

events: Retry the same submission ID with text changed to Delete the card
cases.rejected_counterexample: Success with replaced text, a silently accepted conflicting retry or a second work item.

events: One browser queue durably accepts A then B then C
Restore the bridge and retain stable ownership
Drain without faults
cases.rejected_counterexample: B disappears, C overtakes B within the same queue, or recovery requires assigning new submission IDs.

events: Commit A from alpha.app.localhost
Commit B from beta.app.localhost
Observe each session's implicit watcher/hook channels without explicit cross-reference requests
cases.rejected_counterexample: A foreign implicit queue/context or readiness borrowed from another session; gamma becomes armed merely because a bridge exists.

events: Begin storage of B
Fail the commit before durable bridge acceptance under the chosen policy
Observe the response
Remove the fault and retry B
cases.rejected_counterexample: An in-memory receipt returns success despite failed persistence, or the browser removes B on a failed response.

events: Withdraw A under the supported protocol
Restart the bridge
Retry A with its original submission ID within the retained retry horizon
cases.rejected_counterexample: The retry recreates open work or sends its withdrawal to the currently selected unrelated owner.

cases.policy_dependency: The reviewed supported queue capacity is 25 in the inspected source; keep this example bound to the declared policy if the capacity changes.
events: Attempt acceptance of one additional distinct submission
cases.rejected_counterexample: The oldest prompt is silently removed or acceptance is reported without recoverable storage.

events: A delayed document-1 capture for mark-A arrives after document-2 registration and mark-B publication
cases.rejected_counterexample: A visually valid old screenshot is accepted for the new document merely because the tab URL matches.

events: Request bridge readiness or startup
cases.rejected_counterexample: An occupied TCP port is counted as a healthy bridge, or the unknown listener is killed to win the port.

events: Generate a result report from all three independent attempt records
cases.rejected_counterexample: The reporter says 2 of 2 succeeded, drops C, or treats three attempts as a qualified p99 estimate.

events: Submit A from the eligible browser
Observe watcher receipt of A
Wait without a new user prompt
Deliver an authorized next prompt and observe the scoped context
cases.rejected_counterexample: Watcher stdout is relabeled as actual agent receipt or pull mode is advertised as autonomous push.

events: Late close/error callbacks arrive from connection-1
Deliver a valid current snapshot on connection-2
Submit A
cases.rejected_counterexample: A callback closes a shared mutable current socket or starts an orphan reconnect loop.
